key_terms: The offset of the next record a consumer instance will fetch, which advances as it reads.
The stored offset where a later consumer in the same group resumes. Committing n means the next record to read is n.
Committing an offset only after the record's effect succeeds, so a crash can replay the effect but never skip it.
Assigning specific partitions to a consumer without group subscription, which isolates offset behavior from rebalancing.
The coordinator's reassignment of partitions among group members when a member joins, leaves or fails.
evidence: Actual owned Docker workshop observations, with source, failure and lifecycle scope stated separately. Commands are not executed by the classroom pad.
